groups.reason: Version/help output assertions migrated to portable schemas. A consolidated theory retains the original ShellJson and ErrorCommandState type checks for every command/theory row.

Builtin/path values and all error inputs are covered by portable contracts. Compact C# theories retain exact internal result/exception types; decimal representation, ShellSequence and parser error AST/offset assertions remain in their original tests.

Script path, argument and variable isolation tests migrated to portable contracts. The remaining mixed control-flow test retains ShellNumber result typing and direct function-registry assertions after return.

Observable filter behavior migrated to portable contracts. Retain state/result identity, ShellJson normalization for text, boolean and sequence results, renderer ownership, cancellation-token propagation and CLR exception wrapping checks.
Offline command/result semantics are observable. Corpus links cover only the cited scenarios; remaining assertions and variants await external migration.

Process suite mixes startup, stream, stdin, environment, rendering and error variants. Script/args cases can migrate many scenarios, but stdin/interactive variants and remaining rows are not claimed covered.

Binding/exit-code tests include reflection-only custom target types and exception classification. Built-in CLI binding scenarios are linked separately; internal conversion/classification assertions remain C# coverage.

Write-error tests inject SDK BadRequest/Forbidden responses, earlier-write failures and bounded diagnostic buffers through C# collaborators. These deterministic service failures and internal buffer limits remain implementation coverage.

Mocked Cosmos SDK/control-plane calls, state visitors, request options, resource lifetimes or in-memory command results cannot be asserted equivalently by an offline child executable. Any externally migrated subset remains a partial link.
Update transport/cache/version-selection tests use .NET-specific collaborators and simulated responses, not stable offline CLI inputs.

AST/token structure, direct ShellObject conversion, parser visitor dispatch or in-process interpreter state are implementation contracts. Publicly observable expression subsets can be linked without replacing these assertions.
Tracing, diagnostic logging, redaction helper and serialized-execution implementation tests retain direct .NET instrumentation coverage; observable process behavior requires separate cases.
Live Cosmos emulator connection, resources, queries or writes are prerequisites. Offline corpus cannot replace this behavior; emulator corpus links are partial evidence only.
These suites mix offline scenarios with interactive console, external jq, filesystem setup or connection behavior. Offline links deliberately cover only selected rows.
Explicit benchmark workloads or Azure/serverless account configuration are opt-in environment-specific tests, not offline correctness scenarios.
